issues.description: Constructor 'Lecture(...)' parameter order mismatch: The problem statement (UML and instructions) expects the Lecture constructor parameters in the order: numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors (see UML). The solution implements a constructor with signature: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) (lectureName first, then numeric attributes). The template currently contains a TODO for adding the constructor. This discrepancy can confuse students about the required constructor signature and may cause tests that assert a specific parameter order to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter order consistent across problem statement, template, and solution. Option A (preferred if following the UML): change the constructor signature in the solution and template to match the UML order, e.g. public Lecture(int numberOfInscribedStudents, String lectureName, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfTutors) and update any tests accordingly. Option B: if the current implementation order is intentional, update the UML and the instruction text to explicitly show the constructor signature used in the solution (lectureName first, then numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) and keep template and solution aligned. Apply the chosen change consistently to both template and solution so students and tests are not in conflict.
